[0] At today's "Surprise and Shine" launch event, Apple confirmed the rollout timeline for the all-new Siri AI, which will launch first in English and expand to five additional languages in October. Here are the details.

[1] Siri AI language expansion confirmed for October launch

[2] Apple today unveiled its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple also announced the Apple Watch Series 12 Ultra 4, as well as the AirPods 5 with active noise cancellation.

[3] The common thread across these devices is that they will all feature one or more capabilities of the new Siri AI, which is built on Apple's partnership with Google to deliver a more powerful large language model assistant experience.

[4] Apple first previewed Siri AI earlier this year at WWDC, and today provided a more concrete timeline for language support.

[5] Apple AI product marketing vice president Lilian Rincon said at the event that the new Siri AI will arrive in English when iOS 27 officially launches on September 14, with the following languages gaining support in October:

  • [6] French
  • [7] Japanese
  • [8] Korean
  • [9] Portuguese
  • [10] Spanish

[11] Rincon also confirmed two pieces of information that Apple's Craig Federighi mentioned earlier this year at WWDC.

[12] First, some features will have usage limits due to their reliance on powerful server-side models, with additional usage allowances bundled with most iCloud+ plans.

[13] Second, Apple Intelligence (of which Siri AI is just one part) will support the following 16 languages in this month's operating system updates:

  • [14] English
  • [15] Simplified Chinese
  • [16] Traditional Chinese
  • [17] Danish
  • [18] Dutch
  • [19] French
  • [20] German
  • [21] Italian
  • [22] Japanese
  • [23] Korean
  • [24] Norwegian
  • [25] Portuguese
  • [26] Spanish
  • [27] Swedish
  • [28] Turkish
  • [29] Vietnamese

[30] Apple noted that Apple Intelligence is not available in China, though the company appears to be working behind the scenes to bring the features to that market. Apple also mentioned that Siri AI will not launch in China and the EU, where Apple and EU regulators remain at odds over the Digital Markets Act.
